physicalNotes: Radius 0.18467303 Jupiter radii from Livingston et al. 2018 (2018AJ....156...78L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract): 13,202.6 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0155 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Hirano et al. 2018 (2018AJ....155..127H), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname HIRANO_ET_AL__2018): P 7.95478 d
sources.shape: Livingston et al. 2018 (2018AJ....156...78L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname LIVINGSTON_ET_AL__2018): a/R* 24.9; Livingston et al. 2018 (2018AJ....156...78L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname LIVINGSTON_ET_AL__2018): inclination derived from its impact parameter 0.42 with its a/R* 24.9 (Winn 2010, eq. 7)
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Hirano et al. 2018 (2018AJ....155..127H), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname HIRANO_ET_AL__2018): transit mid-time 2457576.38098 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 396 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
